notation.meaning: X_0 is the source x_1. Predict X_t before revealing y_t; the source explicitly allows the adversary to choose y_t after seeing X_t. The support inequality for |x-y| compares against every real point, not just feasible predictions. At equality all slopes in [-1,1] are legal.

The shared noncomputable selector depends on the current whole loss and point. For these losses support existence makes its default branch unreachable on the played run. Projection is the actual unique nearest point in [0,1]. Prefix equality fixes the external initial state and rates; it does not certify their independence from future data.

R_T(u) is cumulative actual loss minus the fixed comparator loss. T>=1 determines one constant eta=1/sqrt(T) for that run, shared by all comparators. The eventual statement varies T across separately prescribed runs; it gives upper control, not signed convergence or an anytime schedule.

Fix a deterministic external policy p. After predicting X_t, it receives the complete past loss functions, the actual outputs through X_t, and the current whole loss f_t. Write g_t=p(t,f_<t,X_<=t,f_t), and L_T for global-support membership g_t in partial f_t(X_t) for every t<T. No comparator is an input. Prefix equality holds with the same p and initial state. It does not certify independence of their external selection from future information.

worked_example.title: Canonical and history-sensitive absolute-loss runs
worked_example.intro: Take labels 0,1,0,1, initial point1 and eta=1/2, which equals the prescribed rate for T=4. The first three steps retain that canonical example. The policy examples below instead start at1/2 and use one fixed history-sensitive rule.

steps.title: Follow the genuine recurrence
steps.detail: The selected supports are 1,-1,1,-1; every played point is away from its label, so no tie choice enters.
steps.fallback: These are equalities for the shared recursive outputs.

steps.title: Retain the terminal term
steps.detail: Against u=1/2, regret is1, support energy is4 and the terminal contribution is1/4. The sharp fixed-step right side equals the actual regret.
steps.fallback: The negative terminal distance is material to this equality.

steps.title: Read the tuned guarantee separately
steps.detail: The all-comparator theorem gives R4(u)<=2 for every u in [0,1]. It is an upper bound, distinct from the exact realized value above.
steps.fallback: The original canaries also test nonzero legal tie supports, invalid supports, true clipping, strict-prefix equality and zero horizon.

steps.title: Meet at the same kink with different histories
steps.detail: Use eta=1/2. Labels A start at0, labels B start at1, and both are1/2 thereafter. The common policy chooses the unique legal support off the kink; at a later kink it chooses+1 if the first loss at0 is0, otherwise-1. At time2 both predictions and current losses coincide, but the pasts select opposite supports.
steps.fallback: The two histories and all outputs are derived from the same actual recursive policy, rather than supplied as trajectories.

steps.title: Keep the positive terminal distance
steps.detail: Against u=1/4, A has regret1/2 and B has regret0. A has selected-support energy4 and squared terminal distance1/16. The actual sharp fixed-rate bound evaluates to1.
steps.fallback: The negative terminal term remains present and nonzero; the bound1 is distinct from the realized regret1/2.

steps.title: Read the same-run all-comparator guarantee
steps.detail: At T=4 the rate1/2 equals1/sqrt(T). Apply the new public theorem to the very A trajectory to obtain the uniform comparator bound2.
steps.fallback: The exact realized comparator values, fixed-rate bound and tuned all-comparator bound are separate facts.

steps.title: Distinguish played legality from an off-path law
steps.detail: The policy is legal for every played feasible absolute label. At the off-path loss f(x)=|x+1| and current point1/2, however, its rule reads f(0)=1 and chooses-1; the only global support there is+1.
steps.fallback: This disproves the optional universal OracleLaw while preserving legal feedback on the source-game runs.

steps.title: Check identities beyond the performance hypotheses
steps.detail: Change labels and rates from time4 onward to-99: strict-prefix equality leaves the time4 output unchanged. Separately, zero step size from infeasible initial point2 still produces the actual clamp1 at the next output.
steps.fallback: These are total recurrence identities. No source-game performance guarantee is asserted for invalid labels, negative rates or infeasible initialization.

steps.title: Vary the prescribed horizon explicitly
steps.detail: Keep the common policy, infinite labelsA, initial point1/2 and comparator1/4 fixed. Played legality holds for every positive horizon, each using its own eta_T. The new eventual theorem gives the concrete upper threshold1/10.
steps.fallback: The assertion concerns a family of runs and only an upper inequality for signed average regret.

proof_bridge.title: From the full support set to square-root regret
proof_bridge.summary: The source transfers the projection proof to subgradients. The library makes the shifted support equality and quantitative substitutions explicit.

steps.title: Translate the full support inequality
steps.detail: The global supporting condition for |x-y| becomes that for |r| at r=x-y. A change of variables proves both directions, then the positive, zero and negative cases give the complete set.
steps.fallback: The comparison variable ranges over all real numbers. At zero the entire interval remains legal.

steps.title: Produce a valid current support
steps.detail: Finite absolute losses are proper and have a global support at every feasible point. These facts discharge the shared selector interface and prove the norm bound for the actual selected support.
steps.fallback: Support existence and the norm bound are conclusions of the loss analysis, rather than supplied regret or gradient assumptions.

steps.title: Project and telescope the same trajectory
steps.detail: The shared recurrence predicts using strict past feedback. After the current label is revealed, it applies the selected support and projection. The positive constant-step bound keeps its terminal residual.
steps.fallback: The source allows the adversary to see the current prediction before choosing its label. The proof is deterministic for the resulting sequence; the same trajectory serves all comparators.

steps.title: Substitute the diameter and rate
steps.detail: Feasible initial point and comparator give |X0-u|<=1. The support sum is at most T. Dropping the nonpositive terminal term and setting eta=1/sqrt(T) yields the displayed constant.
steps.fallback: Tuning is fixed for the entire known-horizon run. The original label-feasibility premise stays in the statement.

steps.title: Pass only the upper bound to the limit
steps.detail: Divide the finite inequality by positive T. Since 1/sqrt(T) tends to zero, the signed average is eventually below every positive epsilon along the horizon-indexed family.
steps.fallback: Only the numerical envelope is asserted to converge to zero. The actual average may remain negative.

steps.title: Use played-legal history choices
steps.detail: At each played point, legal membership in the full shifted support set gives |g_t|<=1. The actual policy output obeys the same shared clamp recurrence, so the existing fixed-rate proof applies to this very trajectory. No norm or regret inequality is supplied as a premise.
steps.fallback: Legality is imposed only on the actual played path; arbitrary off-path queries need not be valid.

steps.title: Apply the finite bound to a horizon family
steps.detail: Choose eta_T=1/sqrt(T) and use diameter1 and the selected-support bound1. For every positive horizon, assumed played legality enables the finite theorem. Divide by T and pass only the upper envelope to zero.
steps.fallback: For the eventual theorem the policy, labels and initialization stay fixed, while each horizon prescribes a separate run.

notation.meaning: X_0 is the source x_1. Predict X_t before revealing y_t; the source explicitly allows the adversary to choose y_t after seeing X_t. The support inequality for |x-y| compares against every real point, not just feasible predictions. At equality all slopes in [-1,1] are legal.

The shared noncomputable selector depends on the current whole loss and point. For these losses support existence makes its default branch unreachable on the played run. Projection is the actual unique nearest point in [0,1]. Prefix equality fixes the external initial state and rates; it does not certify their independence from future data.

R_T(u) is cumulative actual loss minus the fixed comparator loss. T>=1 determines one constant eta=1/sqrt(T) for that run, shared by all comparators. The eventual statement varies T across separately prescribed runs; it gives upper control, not signed convergence or an anytime schedule.

Fix a deterministic external policy p. After predicting X_t, it receives the complete past loss functions, the actual outputs through X_t, and the current whole loss f_t. Write g_t=p(t,f_<t,X_<=t,f_t), and L_T for global-support membership g_t in partial f_t(X_t) for every t<T. No comparator is an input. Prefix equality holds with the same p and initial state. It does not certify independence of their external selection from future information.
